# lib/auth/

## Purpose
Request authentication and the per-request transaction. `withAuth` (cookie session), `runBearerRequest` in `bearerPipeline.ts` (PAT / OAuth; behind `withBearerOrCookieAuth` and `withBearerAuth`) and `withExtensionToken` (bank-feed extension) each authenticate, open one transaction as `app_user` with the RLS GUCs, run the handler inside it, then COMMIT or ROLLBACK and release.

## Caller contract
- Compose a route as `withAuth(withErrorHandler(handler))`: `withErrorHandler` goes INSIDE the wrapper, so a caught error is answered 500 and the wrapper sees the status and rolls back.
- A status of 500 or more rolls back; anything lower COMMITs, so a 4xx sent after a write commits that write. Throw (or answer 500) after a write, never 4xx.
- Background work goes through `runAfterCommit`; the wrapper starts it only after COMMIT.

## Main signatures
- `withAuth(handler)`, `withBearerOrCookieAuth(handler)`, `withBearerAuth(handler)`, `withExtensionToken(handler)`: `NextApiHandler`
- `runBearerRequest(req, res, rawToken, handler, opts?)` (`bearerPipeline.ts`)
- `deferEnd(res): DeferredEnd` and `answerThrow(req, res, deferred, err, ctx)` (`deferredEnd.ts`)

## Business rules
- **The response flushes after the transaction ends.** Each wrapper swaps `res.end` for a buffer (`deferEnd`), finalises, then replays the one buffered `end` through the real one. Otherwise a client that refetches right after a 200 can read the database before COMMIT. A failed COMMIT turns the buffered 2xx into 500 `COMMIT_FAILED`.
- **A throw is answered by the wrapper, never rethrown (R-159).** On a throw the wrapper rolls back, puts the real `end` back and answers with `respondToUnhandledError`, the same responder `withErrorHandler` uses: 503 for a lock timeout, 403 for a refused Login-as session, otherwise 500 `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`. It also logs and reports to Sentry with the tenant. It used to rethrow with the buffer still in place, so any later 500 was swallowed and the client hung. `invitations/revoke/[id].ts`, which has no `withErrorHandler`, hung on every throw. If the headers were already sent, the wrapper only closes the response.
- `res.end` is swapped only in `deferredEnd.ts`. A new transaction-owning wrapper must call `deferEnd` inside a `try` whose `catch` calls `answerThrow` and throws nothing. `tests/unit/lib/auth/deferredEndCensus.test.ts` enforces all three rules.

## Recent changes
- 2026-09-30 (R-159): the buffered flush moved into `deferredEnd.ts`, and the three wrappers answer a throw instead of rethrowing it.
